title: Check ASCII Palindromic
summary: Given a string of lowercase English letters, convert each character to its 8-bit binary ASCII representation, maintaining the order.
statement: Given a string of lowercase English letters, convert each character to its 8-bit binary ASCII representation, maintaining the order. Return true if the binary string is a palindrome, otherwise return false.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 100; s contains lowercase English letters.
Replace each character with exactly eight ASCII bits, including its leading zero, and concatenate in order.
Return whether the resulting bit string reads the same forward and backward.
hints: The palindrome is defined over bits, so character symmetry alone is insufficient.
Encode every ASCII value to exactly eight binary digits before concatenating.
Build bits, then compare it with its reverse.
Fixed-width encoding preserves every leading zero required by the constructed sequence.
editorial: Fixed-width encoding preserves every leading zero required by the constructed sequence.

tests.explanation: Each f is 01100110; their concatenation is palindromic.
The concatenated eight-bit character encodings do not read the same backward.
